title: Exponential-Family Membership Inference: From LiRA and RMIA to BaVarIA
abstract: arXiv:2603.11799v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Membership inference attacks (MIAs) are becoming standard tools for auditing the privacy of machine learning models. The leading attacks -- LiRA (Carlini et al., 2022) and RMIA (Zarifzadeh et al., 2024) -- appear to use distinct scoring strategies, while the recently proposed BASE (Lassila et al., 2025) was shown to be equivalent to RMIA, making it difficult for practitioners to choose among them. We show that all three are instances of a single exponential-family log-likelihood ratio framework, differing only in their distributional assumptions and the number of parameters estimated per data point. This unification reveals a hierarchy (BASE1-4) that connects RMIA and LiRA as endpoints of a spectrum of increasing model complexity, and yields a practical rule -- match the attack's complexity to the available shadow-model budget. Within this framework, we identify variance estimation as a primary bottleneck at small shadow-model budget

translated_title: 指数族成员推断：从LiRA和RMIA到BaVarIA
translated_abstract: arXiv:2603.11799v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：成员推断攻击（MIAs）正成为审计机器学习模型隐私的标准工具。领先的攻击方法——LiRA（Carlini等人，2022年）和RMIA（Zarifzadeh等人，2024年）——看似使用不同的评分策略，而最近提出的BASE（Lassila等人，2025年）被证明与RMIA等价，这使得实践者难以在其中做出选择。我们表明，这三种方法都是单一指数族对数似然比框架的实例，仅在分布假设和每个数据点估计的参数数量上有所不同。这种统一揭示了一个层次结构（BASE1-4），将RMIA和LiRA连接为模型复杂度递增谱系的两个端点，并得出一个实用规则——将攻击的复杂度与可用的影子模型预算相匹配。在此框架内，我们识别出方差估计在小影子模型预算下的主要瓶颈。
tldr: 本文统一了LiRA、RMIA和BASE三种成员推断攻击为指数族对数似然比框架，揭示了它们的层次关系，并指出方差估计是低影子模型预算下的关键瓶颈。
en_tdlr: This paper unifies LiRA, RMIA, and BASE membership inference attacks into an exponential-family log-likelihood ratio framework, revealing their hierarchical relationship and identifying variance estimation as a key bottleneck under small shadow-model budgets.
